title: Voz pasiva: herencias de la jerarquía colonial

sections.content: A synthesis on legacy needs passive voice to separate what changed legally (a law was abolished, a distinction was eliminated) from what didn't change as fast (structures were maintained, inherited, transformed rather than erased). These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: El sistema legal de castas fue abolido con notable rapidez tras las guerras de independencia.
items.english: The legal caste system was abolished with notable speed after the wars of independence.

items.spanish: Las distinciones legales basadas en el origen racial fueron eliminadas de la legislación en apenas unos años.
items.english: Legal distinctions based on racial origin were eliminated from legislation within just a few years.

items.spanish: Las jerarquías no fueron simplemente borradas por un decreto legal: fueron transformadas, y en gran medida heredadas.
items.english: The hierarchies were not simply erased by a legal decree: they were transformed, and largely inherited.

items.spanish: Ciertas prácticas culturales fueron mantenidas de forma casi inalterada durante décadas.
items.english: Certain cultural practices were maintained almost unchanged for decades.

sections.content: Fue abolido / fueron eliminadas mark a clean, dated legal event; fueron transformadas / fueron heredadas / fueron mantenidas describe something slower and less complete. Putting both kinds of passive sentence in the same paragraph is exactly how you argue that a law changing fast doesn't mean a society changed just as fast.
